previous_statement: Bijectivity and constant choice. At level one the exact source corner decomposition, the direct sum of the four assumed bijective corner maps, and the target addition isomorphism factor gamma as three linear bijections. Thus gamma is bijective, its matrix maps are precisely its amplifications, and choosing universal a_merge and C_merge to dominate the block, homomorphism, norm, and admissibility constants yields an extended C_merge(rho+epsilon)-isomorphism.
new_statement: Corrected obstruction and maximal valid conclusion. Let e_0>0 be the minimum of the universal smallness thresholds in nodes 1.1--1.3. The level-one factorization gamma=alpha_1 Gamma_1 mu_1 is a composition of linear bijections, and the fixed-map hypothesis gives gamma_n=I_n tensor gamma. If one additionally assumes epsilon<=e_0/2 and chooses a_merge=e_0/2, then rho<=a_merge implies e:=rho+epsilon<=e_0, so nodes 1.2 and 1.3 give approximate unit, multiplication, and involution estimates and complete two-sided norm bounds for the raw gamma. They do not make gamma an extended isomorphism: def-extended-delta-inclusion requires exact involution preservation at every amplification, whereas node 1.2 gives only ||gamma_n(X^dagger)-gamma_n(X)^dagger||<=K_hom e||X||. Symmetrization yields a different nearby map and does not show that the prescribed four corner maps themselves assemble to an extended isomorphism. Moreover the root controls rho but imposes no smallness bound on epsilon, so rho<=a_merge alone cannot ensure e is below the thresholds. Consequently the original constant-choice inference and the root contract do not follow from the allowed inputs. A raw-assembly theorem would require both an epsilon-smallness premise and exact involution compatibility; alternatively, with epsilon small, the validated symmetrization branch proves only a nearby-map theorem.
